In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat al-Qamar (the chapter of the Moon), the (surah)

It is also called Surat "Iqtaraba al-Sa'ah" (The Hour has drawn near). It is Meccan, and its verses number fifty-five.

Ibn Kathir said: A hadith related from Abu Waqid [states] that "the Messenger of God ﷺ used to recite in (Surat) Qaf and (Surat) Iqtarabat al-Sa'ah on the two festivals, al-Adha and al-Fitr." He used to recite these two in the great assemblies, because they contain mention of the promise and the threat, the beginning of creation and its return, monotheism, the affirmation of prophethood, and other great aims.

(p-5592)
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

On the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[1] ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split.﴾

"The Hour has drawn near": that is, the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place has approached. As He said: ﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [an-Nahl: 1], and He said: ﴿Their reckoning has drawn near for people, while they are heedless and turning away﴾ [al-Anbiya': 1]. Ibn Jarir said: This is God's warning to His servants of the nearness of the Resurrection and the approaching end of the world, and a command to them to prepare for the terrors of the Resurrection before it overtakes them while they are heedless of it and inattentive. ﴿And the moon has been split.﴾

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[2] ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "This is continuous magic."﴾

﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "This is continuous magic."﴾ Ibn Jarir said: This occurred, as it is related, during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca, before his migration to Medina. That is because the disbelievers of Mecca asked him for a sign, so he (ﷺ) showed them the splitting of the moon as proof of the truth of his word and the reality of his prophethood. When he showed them, they turned away and denied, and said, "This is continuous magic; Muhammad has cast a spell on us." Then this was narrated from Anas, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, and other than one of the Followers (tabi'un).

Al-Qadi 'Iyad said in (al-Shifa): Allah informed of the occurrence of its splitting using the past tense, and of the disbelievers' turning away from His signs. The exegetes and the People of the Sunna agreed on its occurrence, and then he recounted the narrations concerning it.

(p-5593) Ibn Kathir claimed that its reports are mutawatir (widely transmitted) in general. However, al-Shihab transmitted from Imam al-Khattabi that the miracles of the Prophet (ﷺ), other than the Qur'an, were not mutawatir. The wisdom in this is that if they were mutawatir they would be general, and when a miracle becomes general, Allah destroys whoever denies it, as the divine custom has run. The Prophet (ﷺ) was sent as a mercy, and Allah safeguarded his community from the punishment of total annihilation.

Then he said: The reason for their being exposed to mutawatir transmission is that some heretics (malahida) objected that the moon is seen by everyone, so if it split into two pieces it would be transmitted and spread among all people, and no one would be unaware of it, and human nature is eager to spread what has not been seen the like of, and nothing is stranger than this. Yet the implication is not necessary, because it happened at night, at a time of heedlessness, and it need not have lasted long, nor would it have been seen at that time in all regions, due to the difference in horizons. End of quote.

Ibn Qutayba mentioned in (Ta'wil Mukhtalif al-Hadith) that the one who criticized those narrations transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud was al-Nazzam, but he did not transmit his interpretation of the verse according to his view. Perhaps this is the second opinion which al-Zamakhshari and al-Baydawi related, and which Abu al-Su'ud narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Ata' from his father: that the meaning is: "The moon will split," meaning on the Day of Resurrection, "and when the stars are scattered and dispersed." The "sign" here means either the Qur'an, or what they would propose if they were answered in their request.

The meaning of "mustamirr" is: constant and continuous, or firm and strong, from "marrartu al-habl" (I twisted the rope) when you tighten its twisting; or passing away, not remaining, as a self-consolation of theirs with empty wishes; or repelled, because of its extreme bitterness, figuratively.

The clause ﴿And if they see﴾ is either a new independent sentence or a circumstantial clause (hal).

Al-Shihab said: Had this clause been circumstantial, meaning: the Hour has drawn near, and the splitting of the moon in it means its time has approached and its signs have appeared, while they persist in obstinacy, it would have been arranged in the most perfect arrangement, and there would be no harm in it except that it contradicts what is transmitted from the early generation (salaf) concerning its interpretation. So reflect. End of quote.

I say: I have here a point that must be noted: that accusing with heresy someone who denies a hadith whose mutawatir status is not agreed upon is a grave crime and a great error, for the door of takfir and tadlil is not a small matter. Because of this, Hujjat al-Islam al-Ghazali wrote his book (Faysal al-Tafriqa) and refuted with his proofs those partisan people who found it easy to accuse whoever differed from them of zandaqa. By the truth of my life, this is among what has split the word and repelled the bearers of knowledge from getting acquainted with the schools and opinions, until the door of broadening in knowledge became closed, and its circle, after being wide, became narrow; for the books of other sects were abandoned and even burned, whoever collected them was humiliated, and he was accused of innovation or zandaqa, just as many such works pass through the sources of history and biographical dictionaries. Therefore the remaining opinions were forgotten and counted among the anomalous and unaccepted. And when the name of heresy is attached to their sayer, what would become of their status? This, as you well know, is an injustice to the rules of knowledge and a shackle upon thought. Yes! The science of the principles of jurisprudence escaped from them, so strange opinions continued to appear on its pages, though many of them are open to criticism, yet they flowed, striking their ears, and were used as argument against them. Many of the verifiers (muhaqqiqun) have been alert to what we have mentioned and pointed to it in various places; they established in the books of creed that no one from among the People of the Qibla is to be declared a disbeliever.

Al-'Allama al-Fanari said in (Fusul al-Badai'): One who denies solitary reports (ahad) is not to be deemed misguided.

Imam Ibn Taymiyya said: The correct view is that whoever rejects a sound report, as the Companions used to reject it, believing the transmitter erred or lied, or believing that the evidence indicates the Messenger would not say this, such a person is not to be declared a disbeliever nor a sinner, even if his belief is not accurate; for many of the Companions rejected many reports which are sound according to the people of hadith. End of quote.

Al-Ghazali mentioned in (Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din), in the book on the etiquettes of reciting the Qur'an, in the third chapter on the inner acts in recitation, that among its pillars is emptying oneself of impediments to understanding. He said: Most people have been prevented from understanding the meanings of the Qur'an by causes and veils which Satan has let down over their hearts, so the marvels of the Qur'an's secrets are blinded to them. The veils of understanding are four. Until he said:

The second: that one is an imitator (muqallid) of a school he heard by imitation, and is rigidly bound to it, and fanaticism for it has settled in his soul merely by following what he heard, without reaching it with insight and direct witnessing. This is a person whose creed has restricted him from going beyond it, so it is impossible for any thought other than his creed to occur to him. His view has become confined to what he heard, and the devil of imitation attacks him and says: How can this occur to you, when it contradicts the creed of your fathers? So he considers that to be the deception of Satan, keeps away from it, and guards against the like of it. Then he said: The fourth: that one has read an apparent exegesis and believes that the words of the Qur'an have no meaning except what the transmission from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and others conveys, and that whatever lies beyond this is interpretation by opinion (tafsir bi'l-ra'y), and that whoever interprets the Qur'an by his opinion has taken his seat in the Fire. This too is among the great veils. Then he said:

We shall explain the meaning of interpretation by opinion, and that this does not contradict the saying of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Except that Allah grants a servant understanding of the Qur'an." And that if the meaning were only the apparent transmitted sense, people would not have differed about it.

Then he mentioned afterward, may Allah have mercy on him, that the prohibition of interpretation by opinion falls under one of two aspects:

One: that a person has an opinion on a matter and an inclination toward it from his nature and desire, so he interprets the Qur'an in accordance with his opinion and desire, in order to argue for the validity of his aim, like one who argues for the validity of an innovation by an interpretation he invents to deceive his opponent, and like the ignorant presumptuous person who interprets as his desire dictates.

Second: that one hastens to an interpretation based on the apparent sense of Arabic without relying on hearing and transmission in matters related to the rare aspects of revelation. End of quote.

A similar discussion will come in many places which some of the early generation interpreted in a certain way, or narrated what others denied for what was established to them. There is no blame in the arena of understandings, and success is from Allah.

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿And they denied and followed their own desires, and every matter is settled.﴾

﴿And they denied﴾, i.e., the signs of God, after their reality had come to them. ﴿And followed their desires﴾, i.e., what was made attractive to them of repelling the truth, from what they found their fathers upon. ﴿And every matter is settled﴾, i.e., every matter must arrive at an end upon which it settles. It is an allusion that the Messenger must settle at an end, which is manifestation and victory, and that the affair of his deniers is toward humiliation and wretchedness.

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[4–5] ﴿And there had certainly come to them from the news that which contains a deterrent﴾ ﴿far-reaching wisdom, but warnings avail not﴾ [al-Qamar: 5]

﴿And there had certainly come to them from the news﴾, i.e., about the earlier generations and the cosmic realities, of a kind that it would be impossible for anyone other than him, the unlettered one (may the blessings of Allah be upon him), to bring. ﴿That which contains a deterrent﴾, i.e., that which restrains them from what they persist in: denial, heedlessness, and frivolity.

﴿Far-reaching wisdom﴾ [al-Qamar: 5], i.e., it has reached its utmost limit in firm composition and freedom from defect, and in containing decisive proofs and clear arguments. It is either a substitute (badal) for "mā" (what), or the predicate of an omitted subject (khabar maḥdhūf), meaning: "It is far-reaching wisdom." ﴿But warnings avail not﴾ [al-Qamar: 5]: "nudhur" is the plural of "nadhīr" (warner). The "mā" here is either negative (not) or interrogative (what). That is, what benefit can warnings bring to a people who preferred misguidance over guidance, turned away from it, and denied it?

It is also permissible for ﴿far-reaching wisdom﴾ [al-Qamar: 5] to be a new, independent sentence expressing wonder at their condition, given what has come to them that leads straight to faith from the very beginning. This is what is understood from the interpretation of Ibn Kathir, whose words are:

﴿Far-reaching wisdom﴾ [al-Qamar: 5], i.e., in His guidance of whom He guides, and His misguidance of whom He misguides. ﴿But warnings avail not﴾ [al-Qamar: 5], meaning: what benefit can warnings bring to one for whom Allah has decreed wretchedness and sealed his heart? Then who can guide him after Allah? This verse is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [al-Nahl: 9]. Likewise His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101].

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6–8] ﴿So turn away from them. On the day the caller calls to a dreadful thing,﴾ ﴿with their eyes downcast, they will emerge from the graves as if they were scattered locusts,﴾ ﴿hastening toward the caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾

﴿So turn away from them﴾ means: overlook their harm and wait for the severe threat that is coming to them, as He said: ﴿On the day the caller calls﴾, meaning the caller of God, to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, and he is an angel. Or the calling is a figurative representation (tamthil, an image used to convey a meaning) of resurrection, like the command in His saying "Be, and it is" (kun fa-yakun), which is a figurative representation of origination (ibda', bringing into existence). The caller is God, exalted is He. ﴿To a dreadful thing﴾ means: a terrible thing that souls find abhorrent, and it is the place of reckoning, recompense and trial.

﴿With their eyes downcast﴾ [al-Qamar: 7] means: from humiliation and abasement. ﴿They will emerge from the graves﴾ [al-Qamar: 7] means: from their tombs. ﴿As if they were scattered locusts﴾ [al-Qamar: 7] means: in their multitude, their surging and their dispersal. The locust is a metaphor for abundance.

﴿Hastening toward the caller﴾ [al-Qamar: 8] means: hurrying, stretching out their necks toward him. ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day"﴾ [al-Qamar: 8] means: because of the severity of its terrors. And ﴿on the day the caller calls﴾ is an adverbial complement of time (zarf) governed by "will say". It has also been said that it is governed by an implied verb, and it has been said that it is governed by "will emerge". The first view is the most apparent.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant and said, "He is possessed," and he was rebuked (izdujira)﴾

﴿The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant and said, "He is possessed," and he was rebuked﴾ means: he was restrained from warning and conveying the message with severity and harshness, as the form of the verb (*ifta'ala*, the reflexive/augmented measure) indicates.

Al-Nasir said: The second "so they denied" is not a repetition, because the first is unrestricted (muṭlaq) and the second is restricted (muqayyad). It is like His saying in this surah, ﴿So he took the she-camel and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Qamar: 29], for his taking hold of her is the very act of hamstringing her, but He mentioned it first in respect of its generality and then in respect of its particularity, for elaboration (isha'ban), and it stands in the place of mentioning it twice. Another answer here is that the denier in the first clause is elided, indicated by the mention of Noah, so it is as if He had said: "The people of Noah denied Noah." Then He brought their denial a second time, attached to His saying "Our servant," describing Noah with the specific quality of servanthood and ascribing him to Himself by an ascription of honour. Thus the denial reported of them the second time is more hideous on them than the one mentioned first, owing to that subtle point. End.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 54, verse 10:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so help [me]."﴾

﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so help [me]."﴾ That is: my people have overpowered me through their rebellion and arrogance, and they have not listened to me, and despair of them has become firm, so take vengeance upon them with a punishment that You send down upon them.

Then he pointed to God's response to his supplication, exalted is He, with the flood in which they perished, by His saying, glorified is He:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11–16] ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth.﴾ ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed.﴾ [al-Qamar: 12] ﴿And We carried him on a vessel of planks and nails.﴾ [al-Qamar: 13] ﴿It sailed under Our eyes as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved.﴾ [al-Qamar: 14] ﴿And We left it as a sign, so is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ [al-Qamar: 15] ﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16]

﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ means: gushing forth. In it there is a metaphor in the form of a simile (isti'arah tamthiliyyah), comparing the pouring of rain from the clouds to the flowing down of rivers for which the gates of heaven were opened and the hide of the green dome was split.

﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12] means: We made the whole earth as if it were springs gushing forth. ﴿So the waters met﴾ [al-Qamar: 12] means: the water of the sky and the water of the earth ﴿for a matter already decreed﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], meaning: in a state that Allah had decreed and ordained, namely the destruction of the people of Noah.

﴿And We carried him on a vessel of planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar: 13] refers to the ship. Its attributes have been placed in the position of the thing itself, because they perform its function. This is among the eloquent features of speech, as expounded in al-Kashshaf.

﴿Nails (dusur)﴾ [al-Qamar: 13] is the plural of dissar, with a kasra on the dal, or dasr, like saqf and suquf. It means its ribs, or the ropes with which it is tied, or its nails.

﴿It sailed under Our eyes﴾ [al-Qamar: 14] means: in Our sight. This is a metonymy for its preservation through Allah's protection and care. ﴿As a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾ [al-Qamar: 14] means: one who was disbelieved in, namely Allah, the Exalted, or Noah and what he brought, so it is from (kufr), the opposite of faith. Or it is Noah, peace be upon him, because he was a blessing that they denied; it is transitive by itself, and the blessing is metaphorically attributed to Noah by way of metonymy, while the ascription of ingratitude is imaginative or literal.

﴿And We left it﴾ [al-Qamar: 15] means: the story of Noah. ﴿As a sign﴾ [al-Qamar: 15] means: We made it a lesson by which one takes heed. ﴿So is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ [al-Qamar: 15] means: one who takes warning and is admonished. Its origin is (muddakir), with the infix of ta' assimilated into dal.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16] means: My punishment upon these disbelievers, the people of Noah, and My warnings through what I brought down upon them, so that their likes may beware and desist from what they commit.

**The Commentary on the Words of Allah, Exalted:**

﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ [23–32]

﴿Thamud denied the warnings.﴾ That is, they denied what their Prophet Salih, peace be upon him, warned them of. ﴿They said, "Shall we follow a single human being from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness."﴾ [al-Qamar: 24] That is, madness or hardship. So it is a singular noun. It has also been said that it is the plural of sa'ir (blazing fire), as if they reversed the meaning, placing upon their following of him what he had placed upon their following of him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: They said, ﴿shall we follow a human being﴾ [al-Qamar: 24], denying that they should follow one like themselves in kind, and they sought one of a kind higher than the human kind, namely the angels. They said ﴿from among us﴾ [al-Qamar: 24] because if he were from among them, the likeness would be stronger. They said ﴿a single one﴾ [al-Qamar: 24] denying that a whole community should follow one man. Or they meant a single man from their clans, who was not the most noble or excellent of them. This is indicated by their words ﴿Has the reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [al-Qamar: 25], meaning revelation and prophethood, that is: there are among us those more worthy of it according to their claim, because he is less wealthy and has fewer followers. ﴿Rather, he is a liar, an insolent one﴾ [al-Qamar: 25], that is: arrogant, whose pride led him to make us follow him.

﴿They will know tomorrow﴾ [al-Qamar: 26], that is, when the punishment descends upon them, or on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿who is the liar, the insolent one﴾ [al-Qamar: 26], that is, the one who is arrogant toward the truth and disdainful of it.

﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them﴾ [al-Qamar: 27], that is, a sign and a proof for Salih against his people, a test and a trial for them. ﴿So watch them and be patient﴾ [al-Qamar: 27], that is, wait and observe what they will do with her. ﴿And be patient﴾ [al-Qamar: 27], that is, in calling them to his message.

﴿And inform them that the water is shared between them﴾ [al-Qamar: 28], that is, the water they come to for their livestock is divided among them, ﴿each share being attended﴾ [al-Qamar: 28], that is, each owner attends during his turn. For her there is one day's share, and for them one day's share. Al-Shirb (the share) is a portion of water.

Then Allah, Exalted, pointed to their rebellion against the command of their Lord by His saying: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took [the sword] and struck﴾ [al-Qamar: 29], that is, he reached out his hand to the she-camel ﴿and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Qamar: 29], that is, he hamstrung and killed her.

﴿So how were My punishment and My warnings?﴾ [al-Qamar: 30] ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them one single blast, and they became like the dry brushwood of the one who builds an enclosure﴾ [al-Qamar: 31], that is, like dry, broken shrubs which the one who makes a pen for sheep and the like gathers, or like dry grass which the owner of the pen gathers for his livestock in winter. It is also read with a fatha on the ẓā', as an noun of place, meaning like the brushwood of the pen, or the trees gathered for it. This is a comparison for their destruction and annihilation, and that they perished to the last of them, none of them remaining, and they were extinguished and withered, as vegetation withers and dries after the greenness of its leaves and the beauty of its growth.

Ibn Zayd said: The Arabs used to make an enclosure for camels and livestock from the dry thorns.

It is related from Sufyan: Al-hashim (the dry brushwood), when the enclosure is struck with a stick, its leaves break and fall off. The Arabs call everything that was moist and then dried up hashim.

﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will be mindful?﴾ [al-Qamar: 32]

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45–46] ﴿The multitude will be routed, and they will turn their backs.﴾ ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter.﴾ [al-Qamar: 45–46]

﴿The multitude will be routed﴾ means the multitude of the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿And they will turn their backs﴾ means they will turn their backs upon the believers in God when they are routed. The use of the singular "dubur" (backs) is either to intend the genus, or to observe the rhyme (fawasil) and to harmonize with what precedes it. This occurred on the day of Badr, and it is one of the proofs of prophethood, because the verse is Meccan, so it contains a report of the unseen, which is among the miracles of the Qur'an.

﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]. Ibn Jarir said: The matter is not as these polytheists claim, that they will not be resurrected after their death. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time for resurrection and punishment.

﴿And the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]. That is, greater in calamity (dahiya), which is a grave matter for which no remedy can be found. And "amarru" means more bitter in taste; or it is more severe upon them than the defeat they will suffer when they meet the believers in battle.

[47–48] ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness﴾ ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces: "Taste the touch of Saqar!"﴾ [al-Qamar: 48]

﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error﴾ means: astray from the truth in the world. ﴿and madness﴾ means: fires in the Hereafter.

Al-Qashani said: That is, in error from the path of truth, due to the blindness of their hearts by the darkness of the qualities of their souls. "Su'ur" means: madness and bewilderment, because their minds are veiled from the light of truth by the impurities of illusion, and they are perplexed in falsehood.

﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48] means: they are dragged over it.

﴿"Taste the touch of Saqar!"﴾ [al-Qamar: 48] means: its heat and its pain. The metaphor in "al-massu" (touch) is an isti'ara (metaphor) tahqiqiyya (actual/literal-type metaphor). Or, in "Saqar" it is a makniyya (implicit metaphor), and in "al-massu" it is a takhyiliyya (imaginative metaphor). Or "al-massu" is a majaz mursal (figurative usage with a link) by the alaqa sababiyya (causal relation) to pain. The metaphor of "dhawq" (tasting) is well known, and the use of "dhawq" for calamities is as if it were literal. "Saqar" is one of the names of Hell; may God protect us from it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 54, verse 49:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[49] ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with measure.﴾

﴿Indeed, all things We have created with measure.﴾ That is, with a measure in which the requirement of wisdom is fulfilled, and the ordering of causes upon their effects is established. Among this is the creation of the abode of punishment (dar al-'adhab), for what the hands have earned, and the tasting of its pain as recompense for deviating from guidance. This verse is like His saying, ﴿And He created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [al-Furqan: 2], and His saying: ﴿Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1] ﴿who created and proportioned﴾ [al-A'la: 2] ﴿and who determined and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 3], that is, He determined a determination and guided the creatures to it. There is no barrier to this verse and what follows it being a reminder of His greatness, may He be exalted, and the vastness of His power, and that whoever possesses those sublime attributes is deserving of being worshipped alone, of fearing His might, and of being wary of His assault, especially since the caller has proclaimed his warning, and whoever is warned has been given an excuse.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[50] ﴿And Our command is but one [word], like a glance of the eye﴾

﴿And Our command﴾ i.e., that by which existence is brought about, ﴿is but one [word], like a glance of the eye﴾ i.e., one word by which everything comes to be, according to its readiness [to receive existence], as swift as a glance of the eye. Al-Qashani said: ﴿But one [word]﴾ i.e., the connection of the eternal Will, which necessitates the existence of each thing at a specific time, in a known manner, fixed in the Tablet of Power, which is called in the Sharia "Be" (kun). So its existence at that time and in that manner must occur at once. End of quote.

It has also been said: the meaning of the verse is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Nahl: 77].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 54, verse 51:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[51] ﴿And We have already destroyed your like (ashyaa'akum), so is there any who will remember?﴾

﴿And We have already destroyed your like﴾ — i.e., your counterparts in disbelief from the bygone nations.

Al-Shihab said: The original meaning of "al-ashya'" (the partisans, likes) is the plural of "shi'ah" (a faction), namely those followers by whom a person gains strength. Since they were generally of one kind, the word was used to denote what has been mentioned, either by using it in its implied sense (lazim), or by way of metaphor (isti'arah).

﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ — i.e., one who takes admonition from that and is restrained by it.

The statement of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿And everything they have done is in the scriptures﴾

﴿And everything they have done is in the scriptures﴾ That is: in the records (al-zubur, the books) which the guardian angels (al-hafaza) have recorded against them.

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[53] ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾

﴿And every small and great thing﴾ means, of the deeds, ﴿is inscribed﴾, that is, written down, neither erased nor forgotten, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf: 49], and His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird [i.e., his fate] to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [Al-Isra': 13-14]

Imam Ahmad narrated from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: (p-5608) "O ʿĀʾishah! Beware of trivial sins, for they have a pursuer from Allah."

Ibn Kathir said: al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it through the route of Saʿid ibn Muslim ibn Mahak al-Madani, whom Ahmad, Ibn Maʿin, Abu Hatim and others declared trustworthy. The Hafiz Ibn ʿAsakir also narrated it, in the biography of this Saʿid ibn Muslim, through another route. Then Saʿid said: "I related this hadith to ʿAmir ibn Hisham, and he said to me: 'Woe to you, O Saʿid! Sulayman ibn al-Mughira related to me that he committed a sin and considered it minor, and then someone came to him in a dream and said to him: "O Sulayman!"'

Lā taḥqiranna min al-dhunūbi ṣaghīran ... inna al-ṣaghīra ghadan yaʿūdu kabīrā
Do not belittle any small sin, for the small one tomorrow will become great.

Inna al-ṣaghīra wa-law taqādama ʿahduhu ... ʿinda al-Ilāhi musaṭṭarun taṣṭīrā
Indeed the small one, though its time has long passed, is inscribed in writing by God.

Fa-uzjur hawāka ʿani al-biṭālati lā takun ... ṣaʿba al-qiyādi wa-shammaranna tashmīrā
So restrain your desire from idleness; do not become one hard to lead, and gird yourself with determination.

Inna al-muḥibba idhā aḥabba ilāhahu ... ṭāra al-fuʾādu wa-ulhima al-tafkīrā
Indeed the lover, when he loves his God, his heart takes flight and is inspired to reflect.

Fa-is'al hidāyataka al-Ilāha fa-tattaʾid ... fa-kafā bi-rabbika hādiyan wa-naṣīrā
So ask God for your guidance, and proceed patiently, for your Lord suffices as guide and helper.

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[54–55] ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and rivers﴾ ﴿in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful﴾ [al-Qamar: 55]

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing﴾ — that is, those who guard themselves against the punishment of Allah by obeying Him, performing His obligations, and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿in gardens and rivers﴾ — that is, in gardens and rivers. He used the singular form of the noun of genus (ism al-jins al-mufrad) for the sake of maintaining the rhyme (fawasil). It was also read with the ha' (of nahr) pronounced with sukun and the nun with damma, and it was read with both of them with damma.

﴿in a seat of truth﴾ [al-Qamar: 55] — Ibn Jarir said: that is, in an assembly of truth, in which there is no idle talk nor sinfulness.

al-Zamakhshari said: in a pleasing place. Its commentators said: so "truth" (sidq) is a metonymy (majaz mursal) for its necessary concomitant, or it is a metaphor (isti'arah). It was said that what is meant is the truthfulness of the one who gave the good news, namely Allah and His Messenger. Or it is meant that whoever attained it attained it through his truthfulness and his affirmation of the messengers, so the idafa (construction) is due to the slightest connection.

﴿in the presence of a Sovereign﴾ [al-Qamar: 55] — in the sense of a Possessor (malik). al-Shihab said: it is not an elongation (ishba'), rather it is an intensive form (sighat mubalaghah) like al-Muqtadir.

﴿All-Powerful﴾ [al-Qamar: 55] — al-Qashani said: that is, He is able to direct everything in His dominion according to the judgment of His will, and to subject things to the requirement of His intention; nothing is beyond His power.

al-Shihab said: the indefiniteness (tankir) of the two noble names indicates that the understanding cannot grasp the reality of His dominion and His power, and that their nearness to Him is in a station of happiness and honor, such that "no eye has seen and no ear has heard," which is beyond expression and beyond the grasp of minds.
